goal: Launcher checks the exit code after venv creation and after BOTH pip installs, wheels and online (Board gate 171), with the same Fail path: message naming the step, delete partial .venv, pause, exit 1

acceptance_criteria.text: In Start-DataBoot.ps1 directly after `-m venv .venv`: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not create the Python environment (.venv)." }`
Directly after the `--no-index --find-links wheels` pip install: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not install the packages from wheels." }`
Directly after the online `pip install -r requirements.txt`: `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { Fail "Could not install the packages (pip install -r requirements.txt)." }`
Every Fail call comes before the final `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m app.launch $Folder` line, so a failed step never reaches it; each message names its step
The pip install lines keep working when wheels\ exists or not, and nothing in the -Docker branch changes

tests/test_launcher_files.py text tests: splitting the script at `-m venv .venv`, at `--find-links wheels` and at the online `pip install -r requirements.txt`, the text after each (up to the next native command) contains `$LASTEXITCODE -ne 0` and `Fail`; the last `Fail` position is before the `-m app.launch` position

decisions.what: Put each exit-code check on the line directly after its native command, inside the wheels/online if-branches
decisions.why: Acceptance criteria require the check directly after each command; the branches keep the wheels-or-not behaviour

decisions.what: Test checks the single line after each marker, with the online pip marker anchored to its indented line
decisions.why: Splitting on a bare 'pip install -r requirements.txt' text would be ambiguous; the wheels line does not contain that exact string, but anchoring is safer

assumptions: Pip warnings on stderr under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with $ErrorActionPreference Stop are unchanged from before and out of scope for this ticket
